record.paper_title: THE LYAPIN’S NOTEBOOK: A COLLECTION OF UNSOLVED PROBLEMS IN SEMIGROUP THEORY
record.original_question: Determine whether every finitely generated, or finitely presented, semigroup without idempotents has finite chain rank, where a < b means a = ab = ba and the chain rank is the maximum length of a finite chain under this strict partial order, or infinite if arbitrarily long chains exist.

evidence.quote:
Problem 3.11. (A.A. Borisov) Is it true that the chain rank of any finitely generated (or finitely
presented) semigroup without idempotents is finite?
It is proved in [5] that finitely generated commutative semigroups without idempotents have finite
chain rank.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a semigroup. Define a relation $<$ on $S$ by $a < b$ if and only if $a \neq b$ and $a = ab = ba$. This relation is a strict partial order on any semigroup without idempotents. The chain rank of $S$ is defined as the supremum of the lengths $n$ for which there exist elements $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n \in S$ with $a_1 < a_2 < \cdots < a_n$; the chain rank is infinite if such chains can be made arbitrarily long.

It is known that every finitely generated commutative semigroup without idempotents has finite chain rank.

Question: Does every finitely generated semigroup without idempotents have finite chain rank? More restrictively, does every finitely presented semigroup without idempotents have finite chain rank?

Only the commutative case appears to be settled in the literature found. The general status appears unresolved based on the available search evidence.

status_evidence.title: Finitely generated commutative semigroups (McAlister & O'Carroll)
status_evidence.snippet: Structural results on finitely generated commutative semigroups, related to the commutative case where finite chain rank is known.
status_evidence.claim: The commutative case has been studied; the general (noncommutative) case was not located as resolved.
